messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: High-severity: GPU prefill OOMs detected on pool gpu-a-2. 23 container restarts in the last 6m. Trigger: runtime.prefill.oom_rate > 5%

sally_oncall: seeing the alerts, paging now. I'm oncall and jumping in.

sally_oncall: tomo, can you grab the node list and any OOM logs?

tomo_sre: grabbing nodes. running: `kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=gpu-a-2 -o wide`

tomo_sre: log tail from kubelet on node gpu-a-2-17: `OOM killer invoked: cgroup memory limit exceeded; process: /usr/local/bin/serve`

tomo_sre: container logs show repeated: `CUDA out of memory when allocating 6.0 GiB` and then `ContainerRestartBackOff`.

anita_ml: pattern looks like very long prefill requests — token windows ~120k in a few traces. KV cache growth spills GPU memory.

raj_reliability: initial mitigation idea: disable prefill caching for that pool, set `MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS=8192` env and roll to subset of nodes. Can we hotpatch?

sally_oncall: +1 to limit prefills. Maya, can support draft a customer note if there's impact?

maya_support: on it. Which customers are affected?

anita_ml: telemetry shows 3 customers with heavy long-window jobs—most traffic from customer: acme-data (region us-west). Error rate for acme-data requests to that pool rose from 0.4% -> 18% since 8620001200.

sally_oncall: decision: execute emergency mitigation: 1) set routing rule to avoid gpu-a-2 for requests with context > 32k tokens, 2) patch prefilling config to cap tokens to 8k and disable KV persistence, 3) drain and recycle the most-restarted pods.

tomo_sre: applying routing tweak: `rbacctl update route --pool gpu-a-2 --rule 'if context_tokens > 32000 then route: fallback-cpu'` (simulated cmd).

deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-config hotpatch -> set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192, PREFILL_CACHE_ENABLED=false across pool gpu-a-2 (canary 2/20).

tomo_sre: canary pods came up with new env. Initial metrics: OOMs dropped on canary after 30s.

anita_ml: also deployed a transient filter to reject single requests with >64k tokens with a 413 response and clear error body suggesting chunking.

raj_reliability: draining high-churn nodes now: `kubectl cordon gpu-a-2-17 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` then restart runtime on node.

sally_oncall: monitoring CPU-fallback latency — it increases p95 from 220ms -> 1.8s for those huge contexts. Acceptable as mitigation to keep service healthy.

maya_support: drafting customer-facing blurb: "We're investigating elevated error rates for very large context requests; we've applied a temporary mitigation routing those requests to a CPU fallback and capping prefill sizes. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix." Want approval to send to acme-data.

sally_oncall: approve. Add note that SRE will follow up with timeline and next steps.

anita_ml: root cause: uncontrolled KV cache growth when prefill length >> training window + aggressive batching. Repro steps in test staging: `python tests/repro/prefill_oom.py --tokens 120000 --batch 8` leads to same allocation failure.

tomo_sre: created incident ticket INC-8620 with preliminary timeline and mitigation steps. Assigning to raj_reliability and anita_ml for postmortem.

raj_reliability: next steps: 1) implement long-prefill rate limit & soft reject 2) add early allocator check to runtime to fail prefills exceeding safe estimate 3) improve metrics: per-request kv-cache-size gauge.

sally_oncall: handoff: I'm going to mark this triaged and hand to overnight oncall at 8620001260. I will stay on for 10m for any followups.

tomo_sre: log snippet for reference:
```
[2026-03-17T02:47:30Z] ERROR runtime: prefill token_count=121432 pid=2345 allocation failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-17T02:47:30Z] INFO supervisor: restarting container id=c3f2f... restart_count=4
```

maya_support: sent note to acme-data (internal ticket 4287). They acknowledged and confirmed they can throttle long-run jobs.

deploy-bot: Hotpatch rollout completed to pool gpu-a-2 (20/20). No new OOMs observed for 6m post-rollout.

sally_oncall: last check: error rate for acme-data down to 1.6% and overall pool OOM alerts cleared. Marking incident as mitigated; will create follow-up postmortem with assigned owners: anita_ml, raj_reliability.

anita_ml: will start a postmortem draft and include reproducer + proposed runtime patch to trim KV cache after N tokens.

raj_reliability: I'll own the safe defaults RFC for prefill caps and deployment of more conservative kv-accounting.

sally_oncall: thanks team. leaving handoff to overnight. If anything spikes, page the oncall. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitored. Tags: prefill-oom, gpu, hotpatch, customer-impact
